lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Job Readiness: Applications, Resumes, and Interviews
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: building a resume from real experience

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic building a resume from real experience task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner lists every real activity that could belong on a first resume, then rewrites at least four of them as specific bullet points that name what they did and what came of it, entirely from their own genuine experience.
safetyNotes: No fabricated experience, title, or outcome is ever acceptable; every bullet point must describe something that genuinely happened.
materials: adult-or-local: a list of real activities: school clubs, volunteering, informal work, projects, or extracurriculars

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which activity surprised you by turning into a stronger bullet point than you expected, and what specific detail made it stronger?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Bullet point specificity: Most bullet points name a specific action and a real, concrete result. | Honesty of content: All bullet points are consistent with the real activities listed in the warm-up. | Relevance ordering: Ordering reasoning connects to the learner's stated interest from Unit 1. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner rewrite their four bullet points a second time targeted at a specific job title from Unit 1, choosing different details to emphasize depending on what that job actually values.

resources.title: building a resume from real experience worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner lists every real activity that could belong on a first resume, then rewrites at least four of them as specific bullet points that name what they did and what came of it, entirely from their own genuine experience.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact building a resume from real experience decision or action.
Model move 2: List every real activity you have done that could reasonably appear on a first resume, even if it seems minor.
Model move 3: Rewrite at least four activities as bullet points using an action verb plus a specific, honest result.

Model check: Bullet point specificity: Most bullet points name a specific action and a real, concrete result. | Honesty of content: All bullet points are consistent with the real activities listed in the warm-up. | Relevance ordering: Ordering reasoning connects to the learner's stated interest from Unit 1.

resources.title: building a resume from real experience action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for building a resume from real experience.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: building a resume from real experience coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner lists every real activity that could belong on a first resume, then rewrites at least four of them as specific bullet points that name what they did and what came of it, entirely from their own genuine experience.
Coach direction: List every real activity you have done that could reasonably appear on a first resume, even if it seems minor.
Learner prompt: List at least six real activities, however small they seem, without judging yet whether they belong.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: building a resume from real experience complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Rewrite at least four activities as bullet points using an action verb plus a specific, honest result.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Write four bullet points, each starting with an action verb and naming a specific, true result or outcome.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Every bullet point describes something that genuinely happened, with nothing invented or exaggerated.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: building a resume from real experience minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which activity surprised you by turning into a stronger bullet point than you expected, and what specific detail made it stronger?

Success checks: Bullet point specificity: Most bullet points name a specific action and a real, concrete result. | Honesty of content: All bullet points are consistent with the real activities listed in the warm-up. | Relevance ordering: Ordering reasoning connects to the learner's stated interest from Unit 1.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: building a resume from real experience supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional building a resume from real experience condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Bullet point specificity: Most bullet points name a specific action and a real, concrete result. | Honesty of content: All bullet points are consistent with the real activities listed in the warm-up. | Relevance ordering: Ordering reasoning connects to the learner's stated interest from Unit 1..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: building a resume from real experience — complete fictional route

simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g10-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
